name: Oxford Dumplings
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: finely chopped suet

ingredients.name: English currants
ingredients.originalText: Half a cupful of English currants

ingredients.name: heaping teaspoonful of baking powder
ingredients.originalText: One heaping teaspoonful of baking powder

instructions.text: Beat until quite light one tablespoonful of sugar and the yolks of three eggs.
Add half a cupful of finely chopped suet and half a cupful of English currants.
Sift a heaping teaspoonful of baking powder, a little nutmeg, and one teaspoonful of salt into one cupful of sifted flour.
Add the flour mixture to the egg and suet mixture.
Add lastly the beaten whites of the eggs.
Flour your hands and make it into balls the size of an egg.
Boil in separate cloths one hour or more.

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Beat until quite light one tablespoonful of sugar and the yolks of three eggs.
2. Add half a cupful of finely chopped suet and half a cupful of English currants.
3. Sift a heaping teaspoonful of baking powder, a little nutmeg, and one teaspoonful of salt into one cupful of sifted flour.
4. Add the flour mixture to the egg and suet mixture.
5. Add lastly the beaten whites of the eggs.
6. Flour your hands and make it into balls the size of an egg.
7. Boil in separate cloths one hour or more.
8. Serve with wine sauce.
